strings.name: Jeffrey Ullman
strings.role: Computer scientist · Compiler and database theorist
strings.summary: Ullman studies compilers, algorithms and database theory and taught at Princeton and Stanford. His textbooks with Alfred Aho and other collaborators connected formal theory with program implementation and shaped computing education. In 2021 he was announced as joint recipient of the 2020 Turing Award; his public remarks about Iranian students also drew academic criticism.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His database, algorithm and compiler research and textbooks have had a lasting influence on computing education worldwide.
strings.facts.f1.label: Research fields
strings.facts.f1.value: Compilers, formal languages, algorithms and database systems.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Columbia University bachelor's degree (1963); Princeton University doctorate (1966).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Compiler and algorithm textbooks
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Aho and other collaborators, organized methods for implementing programming languages.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Database theory and education
strings.highlights.h2.text: Researched relational databases, query processing and information integration while mentoring researchers.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discussing education in the AI era
strings.timeline.t1.text: Met students in Bengaluru, emphasizing fundamental programming and defining worthwhile problems.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sharing the Turing Award
strings.timeline.t2.text: ACM announced him and Aho as joint recipients of the 2020 award.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Joining Stanford
strings.timeline.t3.text: Became a computer science professor; later chaired the department from 1990 to 1994.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Publishing a compiler textbook
strings.timeline.t4.text: Published Principles of Compiler Design with Aho, an early Dragon Book.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Co-authoring an algorithms textbook
strings.timeline.t5.text: Published The Design and Analysis of Computer Algorithms with Aho and John Hopcroft.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Teaching at Princeton
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined its faculty after Bell Labs and remained until 1979.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and Bell Labs
strings.timeline.t7.text: Completed his Princeton doctorate and entered industrial research at Bell Labs.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduating from Columbia
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned his bachelor's degree before continuing research at Princeton.
